text: Assistant: Could you walk me through a recent project where AI was part of your workflow? User: Recently I helped a retail team refresh part of their online flow. I drafted experiment plans with a chat assistant and used it to summarize a few months of customer messages so we could prioritize fixes. The summaries were imperfect, but saved roughly a week of manual triage. Assistant: What did you trust the assistant to do on its own, and what did you double-check? User: I trusted first drafts of plans and copy, but I always cross-checked summaries against a sample of raw tickets to make sure issue categories were not fabricated. Anything customer-facing was reviewed by a teammate.

Assistant: Could you tell me about a project where you have recently used AI tools? User: I help run a small community program. Last season we used a chatbot to translate workshop materials into a few languages and to draft simple FAQs for new volunteers. Assistant: How did the volunteers respond? User: Mixed. The translations were clearly useful, since we could not have afforded a professional translator. The FAQ drafts needed a lot of editing because the bot sometimes invented local rules that did not exist. I now tell new staff to treat AI output like a rough first draft from an enthusiastic intern. Assistant: Has working with AI changed how you plan workshops? User: A little. I now sketch an outline by talking it through with the assistant, then ask it to point out potential gaps. It is faster than staring at a blank page, but I still rely on experienced volunteers for the nuance.
